audit.why: 52.72% over 643 games. You win the opening and lose the scaling, and the chart already hands Rumble four of the seven stages.
Spikes are placed right: your levels 1-3 before Junkyard Titan matters, your first item, and his two-item AP timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings treat Rumble overheating as his goal and his strongest state — 'overheated Flamespitter', 'hit the overheat threshold so Flamespitter burns you for max sustained DPS'.
audit.why: Riot's Junkyard Titan text separates two thresholds: 'When he reaches 50% Heat he reaches Danger Zone, granting all his basic abilities bonus effects. When he reaches 100% Heat, he' overheats. Danger Zone at 50% is the state he wants; overheating at 100% locks him out of casting entirely. The page has these backwards, which inverts the most important read in the lane. A Pantheon watching the heat bar should be looking for 100% as his cue to all-in a Rumble who cannot cast anything back — instead the page tells him that is the moment Rumble is most dangerous, so he backs off during the one window that is free.
audit.corrected: Danger Zone named as the 50% empowerment state, and overheating restated as the lockout window you engage into.

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon is described only as a slow, and the page tells you to bait Scrap Shield as though it were a real cooldown.
audit.why: Electro Harpoon also reduces magic resist, and he carries two charges, so the slow the page warns about arrives with a resistance shred attached and twice in a row. And Scrap Shield is 6s flat — baiting a six-second cooldown is not a plan, it is back before you have finished the trade, which makes 'trade on his W shield cooldown' unactionable advice. Flamespitter is 10s down to 6s and lasts three seconds, so it is a zone to step out of rather than an instant to block.
audit.corrected: The magic resist shred and two charges written into mid, and the Scrap Shield bait replaced with the heat read.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns, and the ability that actually threatens you late has no number.
audit.why: The Equalizer is 130/105/80s and it is the one thing in his kit that takes ground away from your engage — the mirror at audits/top/rumble__pantheon.json reached the same conclusion from his side. Knowing it is 130s at rank 1 turns 'never let him land a free Equalizer' into a countable window.

edits.before: Rumble's danger window: overheated Flamespitter plus E harpoon slow and R Equalizer zone out-DPS your squishy frame if you fall behind.
edits.after: Rumble's danger window: Danger Zone Flamespitter, two Electro Harpoons shredding your magic resist, and a 130s Equalizer taking the ground.

edits.after: Sit right at Danger Zone heat so every basic ability comes out empowered

edits.before: Land E harpoon to slow you and kite your W-gap and short Q range
edits.after: Land both Electro Harpoons to slow you and strip your magic resist

edits.before: Overheated Flamespitter, E harpoon slow and R Equalizer out-DPS and kite your squishy frame — Rumble reclaims the lane at 2+ items.
edits.after: Danger Zone Flamespitter, Electro Harpoon's slow and shred, and the Equalizer's ground all beat you — Rumble reclaims the lane at 2+ items.

edits.before: Rumble is helpless before his heat builds — at level 1 your point-and-click W stun plus empowered Q simply out-damages a Flamespitter that hasn't ramped. Trade on his W shield and move-speed cooldown, and angle your E (Aegis Assault) to block the Flamespitter cone so his only damage tool does nothing while you strike. By level 3 with W-Q-E up, force the all-in: stun, sweetspot the empowered Q, and E through his harpoon. Don't let him free-stack heat by poking the wave uncontested.
edits.after: Rumble is helpless before his heat builds — at level 1 point-and-click Shield Vault plus an empowered Comet Spear out-damages a Flamespitter that has not ramped. Don't wait on Scrap Shield: it is 6s flat and back before the trade ends. Watch the heat bar instead. Face Aegis Assault at the Flamespitter cone so his only damage tool does nothing while you strike. By level 3 force the all-in — stun, empowered spear, shield through the harpoon.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 stay yours as long as you keep pressing. Bait his W shield and E harpoon, then W-in the moment they're down — his Flamespitter only out-DPSes you if you stand in it without your E up, so always have the block ready. At 6, Grand Starfall is your tempo tool: rather than 1v1 him under tower, leap to a side lane and convert this lead into kills elsewhere before Rumble's items arrive. Never let him land a free R Equalizer to zone you off CS.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 stay yours if you keep pressing, and the heat bar is your clock. At 50% he is in Danger Zone and everything he casts is empowered; at 100% he overheats and cannot cast at all — that is the moment to all-in, not the moment to back off. Electro Harpoon comes in two charges and shreds magic resist as well as slowing. Flamespitter burns for three seconds, so walk out of the cone rather than standing in it. At 6, roam with Grand Starfall.

edits.before: This is where Rumble takes over. Once he has 2+ AP items his overheated Flamespitter, harpoon slow and Equalizer zone shred your low-base-stat frame, and he kites your short Q and single W-gap all day. Your shields don't save you from sustained magic DPS. The lane has to already be won — close it before his second item or you become the one getting zoned. Group with your lead and let your team handle a fed Rumble in teamfights.
edits.after: This is where Rumble takes over. Two AP items in, a Danger Zone Flamespitter plus two magic-resist-shredding Electro Harpoons burn through a frame with nothing to soak it, and the Equalizer takes away the ground your Shield Vault needs — though it is 130s at rank 1, so count it. Aegis Assault only ever covered the front. Close the game before his second item, or group with your lead and let your team answer him.

notes: THE FINDING: the page treats overheating as Rumble's power state in three strings, including telling the player that Rumble wants to 'hit the overheat threshold so Flamespitter burns you for max sustained DPS'. Riot's Junkyard Titan text has two distinct thresholds — Danger Zone at 50% Heat, which empowers his basic abilities, and overheat at 100%, which locks him out of casting. The page has them backwards, and the consequence is exactly inverted play: a Pantheon should read 100% heat as the cue to all-in a Rumble who cannot cast a single spell back, and the page instead tells him that is when Rumble is most dangerous, so he concedes the one free window the matchup offers. Also corrected: 'trade on his W shield cooldown' is not actionable because Scrap Shield is 6s flat and returns before a trade finishes, and Electro Harpoon shreds magic resist and carries two charges, neither of which was mentioned. MIRROR AGREEMENT: audits/top/rumble__pantheon.json independently rejected the _missing-interactions claim that Scrap Shield denies Pantheon's mobility, calling it a derived-flag misfire, while accepting that The Equalizer genuinely takes away an engage angle. I have used only the Equalizer half on this side too, and I have written no grounding claim for Scrap Shield.
